messages:
alex: ran a combined nsys + perfetto trace on the 13B-qat runtime with KV cache + microbatching. observed periodic HBM microbursts when seqlen > 256, looks like thrash not sustained hot path. attaching snippets below.

marta: timeline shows ~200ms windows of 280-320GB/s HBM bandwidth spikes every ~1.2s. NVLink stays quiet. likely local HBM read storms from kv loads.

sanjeev: curious if kernel selector is falling back to the generic matmul for long seqlen. do we have kernel names from the timeline?

jules: can you paste the nsys sample table? short numbers are easier to reason about. also what microbatch config was used (continuous batching window / max microbatch)?

alex: microbatch config: continuous_batch_window_ms=15, max_microbatch_tokens=2048, microbatch_target=96. nsys counters (abridged):

```
# nsys summary (abridged)
Time (s)   HBM_Read_GB/s   SM_Util%   MemCopy(s)   Kernel
0.85       312             72         0.003        kv_read_kernel
0.86       298             81         0.002        matmul_tiled
0.87       320             65         0.001        kv_read_kernel
1.98       305             74         0.002        kv_read_kernel
```

marta: perfetto slices align with kv_read_kernel bursts. the pattern: kv read => short tiled matmul => kv read again. suggests eviction/rehydration cycle around large prefixes.

sanjeev: reproduced locally with a smaller run. when seqlen bumped to 1024 and microbatching on, KV cache hitrate drops ~12% and we see ~20% tail latency reg. without microbatching the hitrate improves.

tara: hypothesis: batching heuristic is aggregating requests across different prefixes causing interleaved KV pages to thrash HBM. options: (A) tighten continuous_batch_window_ms for long seqlen, (B) add affinity-based microbatches (group requests by prefix fingerprint), (C) bump kv prefetch target to keep working set warm.

perf-bot: nsys job 1839001109 finished. perfetto link: https://perfetto.dev/trace/1839001109 (contains full kernel timeline + counters).

marta: small experiment idea: change kernel selector rule so that for sequence lengths >512 prefer matmul_tiled_v2 (uses larger L2 tiling) even if theoretical FLOPS lower. might reduce HBM churn by improving locality.

ajex: typo ? -> alex: copying that. ran quick patch switching selector to prefer tiled_v2 for seqlen>512 + reduced continuous_batch_window_ms=6 for long requests. preliminary: HBM spikes frequency down ~40%, hitrate up ~7%. tail p99 latency improved ~9%.

sanjeev: thanks. can you push the perf trace and the two configs as an A/B so we can run overnight load? I'll run through our regression harness.

deploy-bot: canary deploy queued for 3 instances with tag perf/kv-hotpatch. will run for 2 hours and gather metrics.

jules: ack. after the canary we should collect: (1) per-token HBM BW, (2) KV hitrate by prefix length bucket, (3) kernel selection histograms. small dashboards are enough.

marta: also add a perfetto marker for kv eviction events (we can instrument the runtime to emit a trace event). will correlate to HBM spikes.

sanjeev: running the regression now, will post results in this thread. thanks all :thumbsup:

alex: note for follow-up: if this holds we should update optimize's batching suggestion rules and add a short doc for ops teams about microbatching long-seq models.

sanjeev: quick update at 1839001254: canary shows reduced HBM peak frequency and no p99 regressions across 10k requests. posting full numbers after the run.
